Show ONLY ONE hand-sized rounded triangular onigiri sliced parallel to its broad triangular faces into TWO matching triangular halves. Stand the two halves upright side by side on one small ivory plate, with the cut faces facing the viewer at slight opposing angles, enough gap to see the true cut surfaces. Both halves are from the SAME rice ball and reveal the SAME filling. The rice is plain white Japanese short-grain rice, plump oval grains with sparse clean outlines. A SMALL compact central filling pocket, about 1–2 teaspoons, is completely surrounded by a thick continuous border of white rice including above and below; filling occupies about 15 percent of each cut face. Thin matte black-green nori around the BASE only, visible on the outer base edges, never through the rice interior. Clear instructional cross-section, appetizing and physically plausible. Filling for BOTH cut faces: Cooked salted salmon: distinct soft opaque pale coral-pink irregular flakes, with a few visible layered flake edges. NO mayonnaise, raw fish, red roe or cream; this is cooked flaked salmon.
